subject: Order form commercial clarifications — invoicing entity & late fee treatment
messages:
From: Sara Lim <procurement@cloudnova.com>
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify invoicing entity + late fee language on Order Form

Hi Lukas,

Thanks for sending the latest Order Form draft. Two quick items from procurement and billing before we can issue a PO: 

1) Invoice recipient: our legal team has flagged that the contract references ‘CloudNova Group Ltd’ while our AP prefers invoices to be issued to ‘CloudNova, Inc.’ (US entity). We need clear guidance on whether Redwood can issue invoices to the US entity without a separate MSA amendment or counterparty change.

2) Late fee & withholding: our billing team asked for clarity on the late fee calculation (is it per-invoice or per-amount outstanding?) and confirmation that Redwood will not gross-up for any withholding tax in the US.

Could you loop in legal/finance and confirm the path forward? We hope to get a PO by end of this week. I’ve copied our billing contact in case they want to jump on a call.

Thanks,
Sara Lim
Procurement Manager | CloudNova, Inc.
procurement@cloudnova.com

Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify invoicing entity + late fee language on Order Form

Sara — thanks for the clear call-outs. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Karthik (finance) to confirm the options. Quick summary of proposed approaches so we’re aligned on internal asks: 

- Option A (preferred, fastest): Redwood issues invoices to ‘CloudNova, Inc.’ (US entity). We treat this as an administrative invoice recipient change only — no MSA counterparty swap. Requires a billing addendum and signature (DocuSign).
- Option B: If CloudNova requires the contract counterparty to be the US entity, legal will need to prepare an amendment (longer timeline).

On late fees: we can confirm whether to apply late fee per-invoice (our standard) vs. per outstanding balance. Karthik — do you have the standard language and an example calculation we can share?

Kimberly — noting your earlier redline guidance on tax gross-up / withholding (we typically pass tax responsibility to customer unless law requires otherwise). If there’s a preferred carveout for US withholding, please advise.

I’ll hold on external confirmation until we hear back from legal/finance and will share a short addendum draft for Sara to sign if Option A is acceptable.

Best,
Lukas Meyer

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai, Sara Lim <procurement@cloudnova.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Devon Price <billing@cloudnova.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 12:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify invoicing entity + late fee language on Order Form

Hi all — quick legal review below after scanning the Order Form and the procurement note. Please see attached redlines (ACME_OrderForm_v4_redlines.pdf). Key points: 

- Invoice recipient vs contract counterparty: We can accept invoices addressed to ‘CloudNova, Inc.’ as a billing-only change (no MSA amendment) provided the following is added to the Order Form: a short Billing Addendum clause stating Redwood will accept invoices addressed to the specified billing entity and that parties acknowledge the contract counterparty remains unchanged. This is an administrative change and preserves original MSA jurisdiction/limit clauses.

- Late fee calculation: Recommend clarifying that late fee is assessed per overdue invoice and calculated as the lesser of (a) 1.5% per month on the unpaid amount or (b) the maximum permitted by law. This prevents cumulative compounding across invoices.

- Withholding/gross-up: Standard approach — taxes, duties and withholdings are the responsibility of the customer except where law requires Redwood to withhold. We will not gross-up payments for US withholding unless CloudNova provides tax documentation requiring a different treatment. If CloudNova requests gross-up, that will need executive approval and pricing adjustment.

- Cross-entity evidence: If CloudNova requires invoices to be paid to a US entity but the contracting entity is offshore, accounting will require a short attestation (signed by buyer) confirming the payment path and VAT/withholding responsibilities. We can capture that in the Billing Addendum template.

Next steps I propose: I’ll prepare the two-paragraph Billing Addendum and attach it as 1) a PDF for procurement review and 2) a redline to the Order Form. Karthik — please confirm the late-fee numeric example that we can drop into the addendum (I suggested 1.5%/month in clause).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Subject: Final path: Billing Addendum + PO guidance

Sara / Devon — thanks for the patience. Per legal and finance review, here’s the agreed operational path to unblock PO issuance this week: 

1) Redwood will accept invoices addressed to CloudNova, Inc. as billing-only (no change to contract counterparty). We’ll provide a one-page Billing Addendum that: 
   - Confirms Redwood will route invoices to the US entity named by buyer;
   - States that the underlying contract counterparty remains unchanged;
   - Includes the late-fee language: 1.5% per month (or maximum permitted by law) assessed per overdue invoice.

2) Action for CloudNova: please sign the Billing Addendum (DocuSign link below) and include the customer PO referencing deal RDW-2026-0047 and noting the billed-entity as ‘CloudNova, Inc.’ on the PO. That will allow our billing team to invoice to the US entity without an MSA amendment.

DocuSign (Billing Addendum): https://www.docusign.com/link/abcdef123456
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

3) On withholding: per Kimberly, CloudNova is responsible for any applicable withholding taxes. If CloudNova needs Redwood to gross-up payments, please advise immediately and note that executive pricing approval will be required (may impact timeline).

4) I’ve attached a short payment matrix that shows invoice cadence and sample amounts for a first-year schedule to help AP (payment_matrix.xlsx).

If that approach works, I’ll send the billing addendum PDF for signature and we can expect a PO after signing. Happy to jump on a 20-minute call if helpful — propose 11am PST tomorrow.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
